commitResults.messageBody:
Find results appear only in the main person list and are replaced
when users list all contacts. This makes it difficult to refer to
the latest search while browsing contacts, especially if a search
term is frequently looked up.

Add a compact, scrollable section above the person list to display
names and phone numbers from the latest search. Preserve these
results when the main list returns to showing all contacts.

Keep the section smaller than the person list so the main contact
list retains most of the available space.

Add UI coverage for panel placement, relative size, search updates,
and preservation of results after the list command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add contact-detail conflict check to Person
commitResults.messageBody: Two contacts conflict if they share a phone number, an email (ignoring case) or a non-empty Telegram username. ContactConflict reports the first clashing field and builds the user-facing message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Route duplicate detection through the contact conflict check
commitResults.messageBody: Replace name-based Person#isSamePerson with Person#conflictsWith in UniquePersonList, AddressBook, ModelManager, AddCommand, EditCommand and JsonSerializableAddressBook. Model#hasPerson becomes Model#findConflict, with an overload that excludes the contact being edited, so editing a contact to another contact's phone or email is no longer silently accepted. All three commands and the data-file loader report the specific ContactConflict message; the generic duplicate messages are removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test duplicate-contact rules in storage and end to end
commitResults.messageBody: Cover loading files with same-name contacts, clashing phones, case-different emails, clashing Telegram usernames and legacy contacts without Telegram, a same-name save and load round trip, and a rejected add that leaves the model, saved file and undo history unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Back up an unloadable data file before starting empty
commitResults.messageBody: A valid JSON file rejected on load (e.g. for duplicate contact details) has no retired fields, so the legacy backup did not cover it and the first save after startup replaced it. MainApp now copies it to a unique .unreadable-*.bak sibling through Storage#backupAddressBook before starting with an empty address book.
